Title: April 9, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Study Session

Topic1.Title: Boulder Arts Blueprint update
Topic1.Summary: Staff presented the Boulder Arts Blueprint, a 10-year citywide arts and culture roadmap aligned with the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan and CERG goals. It is organized around seven goals and funded largely through the Arts, Culture and Heritage Tax and the 1% for Art policy. Council asked about staffing capacity, grant funding increases to $2 million, neighborhood reach, the back-of-house services cohort, the 2A tax dependency, Sundance Festival opportunities, and the lack of baseline data and KPIs. Several members supported the direction but asked for measurable metrics, reporting, and attention to artist affordability and prioritization.

Topic2.Title: Facilities investment strategy and recreation center scenarios
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented the facilities investment strategy for roughly 75 city buildings, averaging about 50 years old, with 15 priority buildings including the South Boulder, North Boulder and East Boulder recreation centers. Minimum urgent repairs total about $20 million, while larger modernization projects total roughly $500 million, of which about $400 million is unfunded. Staff recommended prioritizing minimum infrastructure investment with current funds and developing investment scenarios for priority buildings, to return in May alongside possible tax ballot measures. Council questions covered sustainability versus cost, renovation versus new build, fire station consolidation, property disposal, and the unfunded liability definition. Council generally agreed with both recommendations while requesting more financial data and a clearer whole-picture view.
